en: Having paid homage to that Lord, the son of Śaṅkara,
by whose grace this transformation of my intellect occurred,
I shall now describe the conclusion exactly and in due order.

For the sake of nourishment, thee! For what has come into being, thee! Thou art a cock; for the sake of procreation, thee! Do not fear, O Earth, thou who art the place of sacrifice for the gods; for Aditi, [thee].

O Agni, you who are unassailable, today [is the day] for the piercing; O Agni of true life-force, in heaven is Viṣṇu. O Agni, Lord of Vows, this is your portion; O Rudra, this is your share, Svāhā! This sacrifice is yours. O Gāyatrī, you are the prop of Varuṇa; you are the body of Agni. You are a lioness; you are Indra’s roar; you are a lioness; you are firm. You are the slayer of Rākṣasas, the destroyer of secret spells, the self-ruling one. You are the slayers of Rākṣasas. O divine Waters, protect me, the friend. Go to the ocean! Satisfy my mind, Svāhā! You are well-fashioned; you are taken with a support; you are the Āgrayaṇa Soma.

It flows for Mitra and Varuṇa; for the waters, for myself, for Madhava, for thee, for Agni. For thee, who art the swift one, for Agni; for thee, who hast the Gāyatrī metre; for thee, the Vreśī; for thee, the Uśik; for thee, to reach the gods from heaven, Svāhā! Agni with the single syllable, Mitra with the thirteen syllables. This is for thee. O gods, manifest yourselves; ascend the heights, O noble ones! Agni, broad, through Savitṛ the impeller, from the seat of the earth—for you both, O Vasus, may Aditi [protect] thee; for you, O Vasus, may Agni [accept] thy form. 3.
May the strides of Viṣṇu protect me; may he who is before us, together with the five seasons, the draft-ox, and the sovereign, grant me long life.

The earth is the meter, Agni is the deity; with the *āśu* [meter] consisting of nine and twenty [syllables], they praised. The *āccha* is the meter, the thread is the means; you are the threefold, you are the king, you are the *virāj*, you are the sovereign (*samrāj*), you are the self-ruler (*svarāj*), you are the overlord (*adhipatnī*). You are the measure of a thousand; for the sake of the army, for the sake of the swift approach, for the sake of the leaf that brings well-being—these are for the one who dwells among men. *Veḍ*! May there be strength! Twenty-seven [syllables]. You are the ocean; the sun is your law; you are splendor. With the first [verses] and the second [verses], may the Hotṛ worship you with the two horses, with the kindling-stick, and with Agni—the twelve [syllables] of the Aśvins.

*Sarasvatīm*, *catvāraḥ agnim*, *sviṣṭakṛtam*, *devaḥ agniḥ sviṣṭakṛt tvām addhyāt*, *agnaye svāhā hiṅkārāya*, *yate kāyā brahman adhyāyāntaḥ*, *tā ubhau aśvaḥ tūparaḥ adhyāyāntaḥ*, *śādaṃ dabbhir navāgneyaḥ kṛṣṇagrīvaḥ*, *tisro brahmaṇe*, *brāhmaṇam*, *saptadaśa sumitriyā naḥ*, *sumitriyā naḥ*, *sumitriyā naḥ*, *edho 'si iti dve*, *śate catustriṃśat*—these are the endings at the end of chapters (adhyāyas). Now, those with three pauses (tryavasānāni): *sarasvatīm*, *catvāraḥ agnim*, *sviṣṭakṛtam*, *devaḥ agniḥ sviṣṭakṛt tvām addhyāt*, *agnaye svāhā hiṅkārāya*, *yate kāyā brahman adhyāyāntaḥ*, *tā ubhau aśvaḥ tūparaḥ adhyāyāntaḥ*, *śādaṃ dabbhir navāgneyaḥ kṛṣṇagrīvaḥ*, *tisro brahmaṇe*, *brāhmaṇam*, *saptadaśa sumitriyā naḥ*, *sumitriyā naḥ*, *sumitriyā naḥ*, *edho 'si iti dve*, *śate catustriṃśat*—these are the endings at the end of chapters (adhyāyas). To you, O Indra and Agni, I offer this prayer. Before the cruel one [comes], may Savitṛ [protect] you; the Gandharva has invited you. This is your heaven; for the Vasus, I take you. You are a Veda; Agni is light; you are the union. Invited here is this [sacrifice]; for the two intentions, for the two applications, you are strength. You two, O Agni, have not been surpassed; by Aditi, I take you. May it be auspicious to me; the path of heat. By the God’s [will], I take you. Of both, the heaven has eaten the other; anointed with ghee, let the mind go to this. The waters belong to Indra; breath is the waters. O King Soma, Indra and Vāyu, yours [are the waters].

These two, the wind and the horse, have come hither; you are the firm one; who are you? Indra and Agni have arrived. Five [verses] with *sajoṣāḥ*; four for Indra; "O Vivasvat, O Āditya," for Bṛhaspati’s son;
"May he come, the ten-month-old"; "Mount [the chariot]"; three [verses] beginning with *ud u tyam*; "Vi na indra" (three times); here is delight. 5.

The planets are your constant seat; the offerings of strength are Indra’s thunderbolt. O barley, they are yours. May they bring us strength and your sovereignty. The caul of the mountain—O Prajāpati, do not cook [it] for the two Aśvins. Truly, you are the one dwelling in the soil; may you make truth the face of reality. You are the girdle of Aditi. Stand upright! Agni is the head. Honey is this. Do not harm me. Śukra and Viśvakarman—of both, Nabhya and Iṣa, the sixteenfold hymn is Agni the Hotṛ. O Agni, you are heat; you are Parameṣṭhin. To both, let there be homage. Three is the life-span through sacrifice. The name is *ṛc*. 6.
"O sweet one, when indeed you have crushed this oblation, having seen this urine, you have settled upon my form; you are my navel."

"Three gods, O waters; the Aśvins [of] the goat; for Prajāpati thee; Agni is the animal; svāhā to breath! Imā nu kaṇve; agniśca; athaitānaṣṭau; yaṅkrandasī; ā sute; kuta stvaṃ; adhi no dasrā; yuvākavaḥ; daivyā vadharyū; asyedandra; brahmaṇas pate; apetaḥ; syonā pṛthivi; bhūrbhuvaḥ; ahāni śan; dṛte dṛṃha; yamāya tvā; anādhṛṣṭā purastāt; viśvāsāṃ bhuvāṃ pate; yas te stana; gāyatrī chandaḥ; samudrāya tvā; abhīmam payaso retaḥ; svāhā prāṇebhyaḥ; lomabhyaḥ svāhā."
One hundred and forty-one; these [mantras] have three pauses.

Now, those with four pauses: *pratyuṣṭaṃ rakṣaḥ*, *agnīṣomayorujjitim*, *sajūr devenendhānāḥ*, *tvā tryambakam*, *yajāmahe 'ṃśuraṃśus te*, *yā te dhāmāni*, *uśmasi devasya*, *tvāgnīṣomābhyām*, *marutvantam vṛṣabham*, *māhir bhūr agne pavasva*, *uttiṣṭhann ojasā*, *dṛśram asya ketavaḥ*, *yunjanti devasya*, *aham jyotiṣmantam*, *pra etu suparṇo 'si*, *virāḍ jyotir imam*, *sāhasram*, *tisro vāyoḥ*, *pūtaḥ punantu mā*, *pitara edho 'si*.

"Thou art the year; thou art the food for Agni; thou art the vigor of both Indra and [Agni]; for the upright one, svāhā! For Rudra, with a golden vessel—thirty-two," thus these [mantras] end in three pauses. 8.

Thou art black; homage to you! Thou art the eager one (*uśij*); thou art the ocean. May honeyed refreshments come to us for the sake of breath. Parameṣṭhin has spoken aloud; Indra and Prajāpati [have spoken] while being carried forth; Soma and the All-gods [have spoken]; Agni with one syllable; Pūṣan with five syllables; Mitra with nine syllables. The severed wave has stood still; the biting serpents have been bound. Ascend the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), the western, the northern, the head, the strength. The metre is *mā*. The portion of Agni is the *vasūnām-yavānām*. They praise with one [verse], with nine, with nineteen. 9.

"Thus, O Chandas, you are the path for truth by means of the ray. Homage to the golden-armed one, to the tawny one, to the ruddy one, to the one with a complete girdle, to the turbaned one; to the assemblies, to the groups, to the carpenters, to the dogs, to the one with matted hair, to the short one, to the eldest, to the Soma-loving one, to the forest-dweller, to the wise one, to the one of the stream, to the one of the well, to the one of the wind, to the one of the further shore, to the one of the sand, to the one of the enclosure, to the one of the parched grain—first, Agni, today, may he go forth with a good standing. These fifty-six [names] end without a pause. 10.

Now, the middle terminations (*madhyāvasānāni*). "Second," "Thou art a refuge, O Agni," "Victorious in the prize," "Pervasive," "I take," "Giver," "In both," "For Indra thee," "Possessing great power"—these five are the middle terminations. Now, the five terminations (*pañcāvasānāni*).
"Let Vāyu go forth, O Anilanda, at the fifth pause. (12) Now, the six pauses:
"O Agni, those [paths] of yours which are of iron," and "O Gharma, those two [paths] of yours"—these are the six pauses. (13)
Now, there are nine *navāvasāna*s;
the horse is the head of the sacrifice—thus [are] two *navāvasāna*s. 14.
Now, the boundary-markers (*maryādā*).
There are fourteen hundred and ninety-three ending in two;
there are two hundred and thirty-three ending in one;
and there are one hundred and fifty ending in three.
There are thirty caturavasānas, making thirty-two;
there are fifty-six nikhasānas, making fifty-six;
and there are five madhyāvasānas, making five.
There are two [sections] ending with five [syllables], two ending with six, and two ending with nine;
adding all these endings together, the total number is one thousand nine hundred and seventy-five (1975), which is the count of the *kaṇḍikās* in the fortieth chapter.
Thus ends the *Avasānanirṇayaśikṣā* composed by Anantadeva.
